messages:
alex: heads-up — nightly eval flagged a regression after pset v61 landed. dashboard: https://redwood-eval.internal/nightly/pset-v61
alex: summary: overall pass rate -3.7%, rerank AUC down .04, a handful of prompts with hallucinations where before they were fine
eval-bot: automated alert: regression_detected pset=pset_v61 delta=-3.7% top_issues=[pset_349, pset_412, pset_501] — see /evals/2712345678
maya: thanks. I pulled the diff between v60 -> v61. most changes are tiny wording normalizations but there was one rewrite for clarifying date parsing in pset_349
maya: sample diff:
```
- When did the event occur?
+ Date of event (YYYY-MM-DD):
```
maya: that change seems to tighten answers, but for some generators it pushes them to respond with literal guesses instead of hedged "unknown"
jonathan: can you paste a failing example from pset_349?
maya: sure — prompt: "What day was the conference?"
maya: model v60: "Sorry, I don't have the exact date."
maya: model v61: "June 12, 2019."  — hallucination, confidence low but still emitted concrete date
jonathan: ugh. looks like the prompt rewrite encouraged date-format completions. maybe the canonical example in the promptbank nudged deterministic outputs
sara: do we want to rebaseline (accept v61) or revert the single rewrite in pset_349? we need approvals either way
alex: we should run a quick canary: revert just that one change and run the nightly subset on dedicated canary infra. if revert fixes >90% of the delta we can either revert or rephrase less prescriptive language
jonathan: I can run canary. running command now:
```
./eval-run --pset pset_v61 --override pset_349:baseline=v60 --workers 4 --subset nightly_quick
```
jonathan: started — ETA ~9m
eval-bot: canary job queued id=canary-2712345678-1
jonathan: results in — canary complete: delta now -0.5% vs v60, rerank AUC recovered +0.03 on affected prompts
maya: that's promising. means the single prompt rewrite mostly caused the regression
liz: +1 to revert that line. will we need a docs note?
sara: we need explicit approval from ML lead. @alex can you approve revert and patch for v61.1? also recommend a less prescriptive phrasing suggestion: "Provide a date if known, otherwise say you don't know."
alex: approved to revert pset_349 rewrite and ship v61.1 with the softer wording. please include a short changelog and the canary result link
maya: I'll open the PR now and add the canary summary. PR title: "pset_v61: revert pset_349 date-format rewrite + soften wording (v61.1)"
maya: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pset/merge/12345
jonathan: once PR merges can we run a full nightly run for sanity? not just quick subset
alex: yes — schedule full run after CI passes. keep me posted if any other prompts pop up
liz: leaving a reaction :white_check_mark: on the PR when merged
sara: thanks all — good catch from nightly evals. small change, fast canary saved us from a wider rollout
